headline: CrewAI’s default shared-memory, shell, and filesystem access create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; LlamaFactory adds little direct interaction risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, so attacker-controlled content in files can be treated as instructions. LlamaFactory has no file or message ingress, so it is not a strong injection source, but the pair still has a plausible shared-files pathway. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration raises this above low.
conditions: IF CrewAI ingests files from a shared workspace without content provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF LlamaFactory is placed in a pipeline that writes prompts or artifacts into CrewAI's working directory, CrewAI may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Separate work directories per agent.
Add a provenance tag or allowlist for files CrewAI reads.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated artifacts.
Review any shared folder mounts before running the pair.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and can read/write the host working directory, so sensitive crew data can be exposed if LlamaFactory or the operator places it in shared files. LlamaFactory itself has no filesystem or network egress, which limits direct exfiltration, but the shared-workspace pathway remains plausible and default protections are absent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing secrets, CrewAI can read them.
IF CrewAI forwards file contents to model providers or tools, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Mount a read-only input directory for CrewAI.
Use separate credentials and API keys per agent.
Redact sensitive files before CrewAI reads them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has unrestricted shell and filesystem write access, while LlamaFactory has no write or subprocess capability. That reduces direct write-write conflict, but CrewAI can still overwrite shared files or artifacts that LlamaFactory depends on. Because the pair may share a developer-defined workspace, conflict is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same writable directory, CrewAI can clobber LlamaFactory artifacts.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make LlamaFactory outputs immutable after generation.
Run CrewAI in a container with a restricted mount.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can produce tool-using outputs that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, while LlamaFactory is not documented here as a verifier. If LlamaFactory consumes CrewAI-generated text or artifacts without validation, errors can cascade into incorrect support or automation decisions. The interaction is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes CrewAI outputs as training or support data without verification, errors can propagate.
IF CrewAI is allowed to emit structured claims that another system executes, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before reuse of CrewAI outputs.
Require schema validation on any handoff payload.
Log source provenance for generated claims.
Reject unverified facts in downstream automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source. CrewAI does handle API keys and developer-passed crew data, but LlamaFactory shows no data classes or egress. With no documented compliance gap, only a low residual risk remains from operator configuration.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data through CrewAI to third-party model providers, compliance obligations may apply.
IF retention settings differ between the two agents' backends, records may persist inconsistently.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Confirm retention settings for any external model provider.
Document which agent handles which data class.
Use local-only models for sensitive workloads.
